# Flyology RDF

> RDF 1.2 for Ada: streaming Turtle and TriG parsing, N-Triples and N-Quads,
> Notation3, SPARQL 1.1 query syntax, RDFC-1.0 dataset canonicalization, and a
> compact binary term encoding. No runtime dependency and no tasking.

Three crates: flyology_rdf (the RDF 1.2 model and its serializations),
flyology_n3 (Notation3, whose formulas and variables RDF cannot express), and
flyology_sparql (SPARQL 1.1 queries, parsed and serialized, never evaluated).

Design commitments that distinguish it:

- Invalid terms are unrepresentable. A predicate is typed as an IRI, so a
  literal in predicate position is a compile error rather than a runtime check.
- Terms are a flat vector with index references, not a pointer graph, so no
  cycle is representable and traversal is iterative and bounded.
- One scanner serves three dialects, so token boundaries are decided in
  exactly one place.
- Parsing is chunk-fed. Input may be split at any byte boundary, including
  mid-escape and mid-literal, and the result does not depend on where.
- Failures are typed: a code, the grammar production, and a source span with
  byte, line and column at both ends.

Conformance is measured rather than claimed. Harnesses read the W3C manifests
with the library's own parser and report what they examined: RDF 1.1 and 1.2
(1050 entries), RDFC-1.0 (86), Notation3 (1070 entries the working group
stands behind), SPARQL 1.1 syntax (488). Zero divergences in each. A
differential additionally compares against oxigraph and Jena across 2,443
documents, asking whether another implementation reads what this one writes.

- [Guide](https://rdf.flyology.org/guide/)
- [API reference](https://rdf.flyology.org/api/)
